Coastal city votes to rebuild the seawall before winter storms arrive

By Maria Alvarez · October 14 · 6 min read

The city council voted 6 to 1 on Tuesday to rebuild the aging seawall along the eastern harbor, ending a two-year dispute over how much protection the waterfront deserves ahead of the winter storm season.

Engineers told the council that the current wall, built in 1978, no longer meets the safety standard for waves that now routinely top four meters during seasonal storms.

Construction is scheduled to start in March and should take about eighteen months, according to the public works department. The project will be paid for with a mix of municipal bonds and a state resilience grant.

What to expect

Residents of the harbor district will see detours along the promenade for the first six months. The city has promised to keep the fish market open throughout, though deliveries will shift to the north gate.

"We cannot wait for the next storm to prove the point," council member Diane Ortiz said before the vote. "Every year we delay, the bill gets larger and the risk gets harder to insure."
